newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremen cotton exchange sees active nearby trades.
newsitem.headline: Bremen cotton exchange sees active nearby trades.

text.p: European spinning mills were seeking high quality spot cottons in active buying, the Bremen Cotton Exchange's fortnightly report said on Monday.
Domestic consumers and those in central and eastern Europe needed replacement cover as yarn prices were rising, it said.
Supply of suitable origins remained tight.
Bremen cotton stocks rose by 2,104 bales in the fortnight ended Nov 29 to 27,508 bales compared with 45,056 bales recorded a year ago.
The Exchange reported upland cotton trades in Central Asian standards 1, 2 and 3, Greek high and medium grades, Turkish lower grades and West African descriptions for spot through third quarter 1997.
Extra long staple trades included Egyptian Giza 77, U.S. and Israel Pima, and Sudan Barakat for a variety of dates through to third quarter 1997.
